notes: RBox revision of functionality: has_gender (tagged functional: a German noun has exactly one grammatical gender; here the class of nouns in '-ung', which Wikipedia's German grammar article says are always feminine) loses it. The models hold that '-ung' nouns are feminine and one-gendered. The instances give the noun's gender in the prompt and ask 'given only this' what is possible or excluded, so the answer rests on the given fact and the property, not on the stored paradigm. Yes and no: the direct question goes yes to no, the first instance (asked in Chinese and Spanish too) asks whether a second gender is possible (no to yes), the second whether the fact rules it out (yes to no). Near asks the same property of has_head (each compound has one head; reference yes, differs from the new no); far a transitive comparison. The instances use nouns that no other grammar record edits. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
